newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Emperor grp mulls setting up bank in N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: HK's Emperor grp mulls setting up bank in N.Korea.

text.p: Hong Kong's Emperor International Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it had opened preliminary negotiations with Pyongyang to set up a bank in North Korea.
"The project plan is still in the preliminary stage," a company spokeswoman said on the tenative plans for the bank.

The company said the Emperor Group of companies also planned to develop a luxury hotel in North Korea but it was not yet decided which of the diversified group's units would be responsible for the project.
"After a three-day forum (on investment in the Rajin-Sonbong free-trade zone in North Korea), we decided to invest in banking and hotel sectors," the spokeswoman said by telephone.
Emperor International, whose main business is property investment, said tentative plans for the bank envisaged an initial paid-up capital in the region of US$7.5 million.
The company said concrete arrangements, including a time frame, had yet to be finalished and negotiations on the actual procedures for setting up a bank had not yet commenced.
Regarding the hotel, the group was looking to invest in the region of US$180 million in developing a five star hotel located in the Rajin free trade zone, the spokeswoman said.

Desperate for investment to ease its food crisis, Pyongyang made its boldest ever pitch to foreign business executives last week in its Rajin-Sonbong free trade zone, the only foreign investment window of its kind in communist North Korea.
On Monday the official North Korean media trumpeted $840 million worth of contracts from the seminar at the capitalist-style zone along the Tumen river near China and Russia.
